    14  # Gaussian integers
    15  
    16  The Gaussian integers are complex integer, complex numbers whose real and imaginary parts are both
    17  integers.
    18  
    19  ## Main definitions
    20  
    21  The Euclidean domain structure on `ℤ[i]` is defined in this file.
    22  
    23  The homomorphism `GaussianInt.toComplex` into the complex numbers is also defined in this file.
    24  
    25  ## See also
    26  
    27  See `NumberTheory.Zsqrtd.QuadraticReciprocity` for:
    28  * `prime_iff_mod_four_eq_three_of_nat_prime`:
    29    A prime natural number is prime in `ℤ[i]` if and only if it is `3` mod `4`
    30  
    31  ## Notation
    32  
    33  This file uses the local notation `ℤ[i]` for `GaussianInt`
    34  
    35  ## Implementation notes
    36  
    37  Gaussian integers are implemented using the more general definition `Zsqrtd`, the type of integers
    38  adjoined a square root of `d`, in this case `-1`. The definition is reducible, so that properties
    39  and definitions about `Zsqrtd` can easily be used.
